To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Arabic-to-Europe translation is more challenging than Europe-to-Arabic; (2) the best performing systems in the Europe-to-Arabicsubset are not the best performing systems for Arabic-to-Europe; and (3) there is a significant difference in performance between systems trained with Europeto-Arabic data only, and systems that are trained on both Arabic-to-Europe and Europe-to-Arabice data.

(a) the best performing system for Arabic-English is the one that uses a combination of neural and statistical machine translation (SMT), (b) the best performing systems for Arabic-French are the ones that use SMT and the one that uses neural machine translation, and (c) the best performing translation direction is from Arabic to French, while the worst performing direction is from Arabic into English.

(1) the best performing systems for translating from Arabic into European languages are those that are trained on the parallel corpus we created, and that (2) the best performing system for translating from European languages into Arabic is one that is trained on a combination of the parallel corpora we created and the parallel corpora used in the WMT shared task.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (i) creating a large publicly available parallel corpus for Arabic and European languages, (ii) evaluating the state of the art of machine translation for 22 European language pairs with Arabic, and (iii) evaluating the state-of-the-art machine translation systems for 22 European and Arabic.
the development of a large parallel corpus for evaluating machine translation (MT) between Arabic and European languages.

the following two questions: (i) What is the quality of machine translation systems translating to and from European languages? (ii) What is the impact of the directionality of translation (from English to Arabic vs. from Arabic to English) on machine translation quality?

the best systems are still not able to achieve human-level performance on translating from Arabic to any European language, and from European languages to Arabic.
, in general, the best systems for each language direction (Arabic to X and X to Arabic) are different, and there is no single best performing system for all language pairs.
there is a lot of room for improvement in translating to and from the Arabic language.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best machine translation system is still far behind human translation quality, and that the quality of the translation depends on both the source language as well as the target language.
